driver: throwaway agy sessions in a scratch git directory: nine agy -p runs with --output-format stream-json (five of them --conversation resumes, three cut by --print-timeout) and one interactive session driven through tmux; transcripts read afterwards, SQLite stores read from copies
scope: Field names, value types, counts, timings, and the harness's own fixed wording and closed vocabularies. No condition, model reply, path, conversation id or typed word; <condition>, <time>, <duration> and <n> stand where a value was.

note: the only place the condition is held apart from the continuation's quote; a /goal input differs from a plain direction only by its request prefix and the [Slash Command] metadata
slash_metadata_fixed_wording:
<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>
The current local time is: <time>.

The user has mentioned some items in the form @[ITEM]. Here is extra information about the items that were mentioned by the user, in the order that they appear:

/goal is a [Slash Command]:
The user has marked this task with /goal, indicating that this task is intended to run for a long time without user input, e.g. overnight. You should be extra thorough and only stop when you are confident the goal has been completely fulfilled. The system will force you to continue execution, prompting you to audit your work until completion. Once complete, include <!-- GOAL_COMPLETE --> in your response. If the user explicitly asked to stop or cancel this goal, include <!-- GOAL_CANCELLED --> in your response to cancel the goal.
</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>

fixed_wording:
The following is a <SYSTEM_MESSAGE> not actually sent by the user. It is provided by the system as important information to pay attention to.

<SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
Stop hook blocked termination: You are still working toward the user's goal. Do not stop until the task is fully complete.

Time spent so far: <duration>
Continuation: #<n>

Before concluding, verify your work:
1. Re-read the original request and identify every concrete deliverable.
2. Build a checklist that maps every explicit requirement and deliverable to concrete evidence.
3. For each deliverable, confirm it is done by checking actual output: file contents, test results, build logs, etc.
4. Wanting to be done or having spent effort is not the same as being done. Only real evidence counts.
5. If anything is unfinished or unverified, keep going. If anything is uncertain, then spend more time to validate.

Once every deliverable is genuinely complete, include <!-- GOAL_COMPLETE --> in your response to signal you are finished.

If the user explicitly asked to stop or cancel this goal, include <!-- GOAL_CANCELLED --> in your response to cancel the goal.

If there is still work to do, take the next step now.

Original request: <condition>
</SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
note: the forced continuation; it shares type and source with the resume notice below, so only the wording 'Stop hook blocked termination:' tells them apart
time_spent_counts_from: the /goal input, across a --print-timeout cut and a --conversation resume (26s on the resumed turn); restarts at a replacing /goal (3s)

interactive_rendering: the marker is not shown in the TUI pane
marker_written_by: the model, in its reply text; no harness record follows it
note: the model repeated GOAL_COMPLETE in a follow-up turn after its goal was already met, so a marker alone does not prove a goal was active

fixed_wording:
The following is a <SYSTEM_MESSAGE> not actually sent by the user. It is provided by the system as important information to pay attention to.

<SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
[Message] timestamp=<time> sender=system priority=MESSAGE_PRIORITY_LOW content=[Notice] All your subagents and background tasks have been stopped due to server restart. If you want a subagent to continue working, it needs to be revived by sending it a new message. If resuming work, please check on status and restart as needed.
</SYSTEM_MESSAGE>
position: immediately after the resumed USER_INPUT, same created_at second

run: a goal met after two continuations, then --conversation with a plain prompt
a goal cut by --print-timeout, then --conversation with a plain request to cancel it, then a further plain resume

note: steps in flight at the cut are never written to either transcript; the next index continues past them
run: a goal cut by --print-timeout, then --conversation with an unrelated prompt

interactive_queueing: two consecutive USER_INPUT records 4 s apart with no response between them; one reply answered the second
note: replacing is silent: nothing marks the first goal ended, and only the continuation's Original request shows which condition is active
runs: print mode: a second /goal sent by --conversation while the first was active
interactive: a second /goal typed while the first turn was still working

recorded_as: a plain USER_INPUT whose request begins with /edit_goal and whose metadata has no [Slash Command] entry

completion_list_fixed_wording./goal: Run until the specified goal is completely finished.

note: a middle cut, not a prefix cut: the /goal line and the [Slash Command] metadata both survive, and the condition loses its middle; conditions were ASCII, so bytes and characters were not told apart
transcript_full_jsonl: whole condition, less a trailing space

transcript_jsonl.cut: first 2048 characters + \n<truncated N bytes>\n + last 2048 characters

num_turns_counts: USER_INPUT records in the conversation; continuations are not counted (1 for a turn with two continuations)
print_timeout_stderr_fixed_wording: [agy] print timeout after <duration> with turn in progress; returning partial output

read: a copy; a read-only open of the live file failed mid-session

goal_wording_found_in: steps rows (protobuf payloads of the same records the transcript holds) and one gen_metadata row
note: no record there that the transcript lacks was found

not_captured: Compass's own agy hook payloads (the plugin is not installed in this agy; agy plugin list showed none)
a continuation counter above #1, or any limit on continuations
a goal the harness gives up on
cancelling with Esc or a typed request in the interactive session
a non-ASCII condition, which would tell the cut's bytes from characters
run_order: agy -p /goal needing several replies (two continuations, then met)
--conversation resume of the met goal with a plain prompt
agy -p /goal of long file work cut by --print-timeout, --conversation asking to cancel, --conversation plain resume
interactive tmux session: /goal met in one reply, /edit_goal, a /goal needing two replies with a second /goal typed while it ran
agy -p /goal cut by --print-timeout, --conversation unrelated prompt, --conversation second /goal
agy -p /goal with a 3,500- and a 5,000-character condition
